jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: Director, Portfolio Strategy & Product Marketing

REPORTS TO: Chief Product Officer

STATUS: Full time, Exempt

LOCATION: Remote

SALARY RANGE: $220,000/year based on experience & qualifications

EQUITY ELIGIBILITY: Eligible for company stock options as part of the overall compensation package, subject to plan terms.

BONUS ELIGIBILITY: Performance-based annual incentive

BENEFITS: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, optional FSA/HSA, 401k with 6% employer match, life and AD&D insurance, Employee Assistance Program, short & long term disability, tuition reimbursement, 21.67 days of paid time off + 10 holidays

About Tidal Vision

We believe that sustainability should not require customers to compromise on price, convenience, or performance. Our mission is to create positive & systemic impact for the critical industries that sustain life. We value innovation and take pride in challenging the status-quo; we choose to view obstacles as opportunities. We value new ideas and encourage the team to apply creativity and invent new solutions to meet challenging demands. We foster open, direct communication, and a collaborative working environment through our unique approach to work culture. We value our employees and demonstrate that through our compensation and benefits programs and opportunities for growth and development.

About Tidal Grow AgriScience

Tidal Grow AgriScience develops next-generation agricultural technologies designed to improve crop performance, nutrient efficiency, and grower profitability. By translating advanced chitosan science into practical, scalable products, we create innovative agricultural solutions that integrate seamlessly into modern farming operations to deliver higher yields with more efficient inputs.

About Tidal Vision’s Unique Work Culture

Tidal Vision strives to build and invest in the highest performing and most innovative team. We put our people and customers above process, avoid company-wide rules as much as possible, and have the courage to take unusual approaches to advance our mission. With this approach, we believe we can create a more flexible, fun, stimulating, creative, collaborative, and innovative organization.

Our commitment to developing, practicing and promoting direct and open communication, responsibility and freedom, and leading with and seeking context is a responsibility for every role at Tidal Vision.

Job Summary

The Director, Portfolio Strategy & Product Marketing leads the commercial strategy and market success of Tidal Grow AgriScience’s product portfolio. The role owns segmentation, targeting, positioning, pricing, channel strategy, label and claims strategy, launch planning, and lifecycle commercialization.

This role is a critical member of the Product organization, working alongside Product Management and R&D to shape and commercialize Tidal Grow AgriScience's product portfolio. As the portfolio's commercial leader, the Director drives market strategy, positioning, pricing, channel strategy, launch planning, and lifecycle commercialization to ensure products achieve successful market adoption and long-term growth.

Essential Job Functions

Lead portfolio commercialization strategy across crop nutrition, biostimulant, and crop protection markets.
Own segmentation, targeting, positioning, value propositions, pricing architecture, and channel strategy.
Own the commercial direction of each product from development through launch and lifecycle management.
Own label and claims strategy, partnering with Regulatory on registrations, substantiation, and compliance.
Partner with Product Managers to translate technical capabilities, efficacy data, and customer needs into commercially successful products.
Partner with Marketing to establish promotional strategy, message hierarchy, proof points, and sales-enablement priorities; Marketing owns creative development and execution.
Build market, customer, competitive, pricing, and channel intelligence into portfolio plans, business cases, forecasts, and commercialization decisions.
Work with the Chief Product Officer on product vision, roadmap priorities, portfolio architecture, and investment decisions.
Align Product Management, R&D, Commercial Ag Science, Regulatory, Marketing, Sales, and Operations around commercialization plans and market outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, agronomy, agricultural economics, marketing, business, crop science, or a related field.
At least 15 years of progressive experience in agricultural product marketing, portfolio strategy, product management, market development, or commercial leadership.
Commercial leadership experience across both crop nutrition/fertilizer and crop protection.
Proven success leading segmentation, positioning, pricing, channel, launch, lifecycle, and portfolio strategies for agricultural products.
Strong understanding of grower economics, agricultural distribution, retail channels, product labels, claims, and commercialization requirements.
Ability to translate technical and field-performance data into differentiated value propositions and commercially compelling strategies.
Strong financial acumen and experience developing value-based pricing, channel economics, and product business cases.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive decisions without direct authority.
Executive-level communication, judgment, and presence.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or advanced degree in agribusiness, marketing, agricultural economics, agronomy, or a related field.
Experience leading a multi-product portfolio within an established agricultural input company.
Experience launching and scaling innovative or technically differentiated agricultural products.
Experience across distributor, retailer, and direct-to-grower channels.
Success operating in an entrepreneurial or rapidly scaling business.

Licensing & Special Requirements

Align with Global teams to ensure consistency while adapting locally

jobs.title: Director of Cloud Marketing
jobs.description:
VAST Data is building a new category — the Operating System for AI
— unifying storage, database, virtualization, and AI services into a single software platform. The world's most innovative organizations rely on VAST to power AI factories, real-time analytics, and mission-critical applications at exabyte scale.

We are seeking a Head of Cloud Marketing
to lead VAST's global cloud marketing strategy across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and emerging cloud providers. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for establishing VAST as the foundational data platform for the next generation of cloud and AI infrastructure.

This leader will own the global cloud marketing agenda, combining strategic positioning, executive evangelism, partner go-to-market programs, and demand generation to accelerate VAST's adoption across the cloud ecosystem.

A central priority will be developing and launching a global neocloud program designed to aggressively expand VAST's presence across AI-focused cloud providers. The role will also drive joint marketing initiatives with major hyperscalers and expand VAST's reach into emerging and sovereign cloud markets.

Reporting directly to the global marketing leadership team, this individual will lead a focused cloud product marketing function and orchestrate a cross-functional, global team spanning field marketing, demand generation, partner marketing, and program investment.

THE ROLE

﻿

﻿Own Global Cloud Marketing Strategy: Develop and execute VAST's worldwide marketing strategy across AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, neoclouds, and sovereign cloud providers, driving awareness, market positioning, partner engagement, and adoption.
Build and Launch the Global Neocloud Program: Lead the marketing strategy and execution of a major neocloud initiative, including partner acquisition campaigns, promotional programs, market development funds (MDF), and scalable go-to-market motions designed to establish VAST across the global neocloud ecosystem.
Drive Hyperscaler Marketing and Joint GTM: Build strategic marketing programs with major hyperscalers, aligning messaging, co-marketing initiatives, partner campaigns, and field execution to accelerate pipeline and strengthen VAST's cloud market presence.
Lead Market Positioning and Executive Evangelism: Shape the narrative for VAST as the Operating System for AI across cloud environments. Serve as a visible market evangelist, developing thought leadership, executive messaging, industry engagement, and compelling value propositions for cloud providers and their customers.
Lead Cloud Product Marketing: Oversee cloud-focused product marketing, translating VAST's technical capabilities, roadmap, and partner integrations into differentiated positioning, solution messaging, sales enablement, and go-to-market programs.
Orchestrate Global Demand Generation: Lead a virtual team of regional field marketers and cross-functional partners to execute coordinated cloud campaigns across North America and international markets, ensuring measurable pipeline contribution and partner activation.
Own Program Strategy and Investment: Partner with Finance, Alliances, and Marketing leadership to structure and optimize cloud marketing investments, MDF programs, campaign budgets, and partner incentives, ensuring scalable execution and measurable business impact.
Build and Scale the Cloud Marketing Function: Develop a focused, high-performing organization, establishing clear priorities, cross-functional alignment, and a scalable operating model as VAST's global cloud business expands.

Requirements:

10+ years of B2B technology marketing experience, including significant leadership experience in cloud, enterprise infrastructure, AI platforms, or data technologies.
Proven cloud ecosystem expertise, with a strong understanding of hyperscaler partnerships, neoclouds, cloud service providers, and the evolving AI infrastructure landscape.
Demonstrated success building global partner marketing and GTM programs, including joint campaigns, partner activation, co-marketing, and market development initiatives.
Strong product marketing and technical credibility, with the ability to translate complex cloud architectures, AI infrastructure capabilities, and platform technologies into compelling market narratives and business value.
Executive presence and evangelism capabilities, including experience influencing senior technology leaders, representing a company externally, and shaping market perception through thought leadership and strategic communications.
Experience leading global, cross-functional teams, including direct reports and matrixed organizations spanning product marketing, field marketing, demand generation, and alliances.
Strong commercial orientation, with a track record of connecting marketing strategy and investment to partner adoption, pipeline creation, and revenue growth.
Entrepreneurial, builder mentality, with the ability to launch new programs, establish operating models, navigate ambiguity, and execute effectively in a fast-growing organization.

Report on performance, budget, and ROI to marketing and executive leadership on a regular cadence.

Proven results running tradeshow and event programs at scale, including major industry events and sponsorships.
Experience in the telecommunications industry, with direct experience working with technology solution distributors (TSDs) to build programs, drive partner-sourced pipeline, and grow revenue.
Experience working with agents, resellers, and MSP or SI partners.
Strong understanding of enterprise sales cycles, the buyer's journey, and the channel business model.
Strong financial skills, including budget ownership, MDF management, and ROI analysis.
Metric-driven, with the ability to draw insight from complex marketing data.
Proficiency with Salesforce, Marketo, and Google Workspace or Microsoft Office.
Excellent communication and influence skills, with the ability to work with executives, sales leaders, and partners.
Strategic, positive, and energetic, with a fail-fast mindset and a strong work ethic.

jobs.title: Marketing Events Manager
jobs.description:
Engineering moves at software speed. Manufacturing doesn't. Yet.

Machina Labs is changing that. We build intelligent, software-defined factories that produce complex metal structures directly from digital design. By integrating advanced metal forming, robotics, and automated production inside a flexible factory architecture, we enable customers to move from prototype to production in weeks, not years.

Backed by Lockheed Martin, Toyota, and NVIDIA, we're building the manufacturing infrastructure that defense, aerospace, and advanced mobility programs will run on.

If you want to work on hard problems that matter and see them fly, drive, and defend, this is the place.

Job Description

Most companies bring banners and brochures to events. We have robots, factories, vehicles, and precision-formed metal. We want someone who knows what to do with them.

This is a unique opportunity to turn the physical world of Machina Labs into unforgettable experiences. Bring customers into our factories. Bring our factories to customers. Create product launches, demonstrations, and activations that make people see what's possible when you rethink how things are made.

We're looking for a creative builder who sees a factory floor as a showroom, a robot as a centerpiece, and a formed piece of metal as an opportunity to tell a story. Someone equally comfortable imagining an ambitious activation and figuring out how to get a vehicle, missile, or industrial robot onto a show floor.

This is not a conventional events role. You'll work in complex, high-friction environments where engineering, production, logistics, and compliance all matter. The right person is resourceful, organized, creatively ambitious, and relentlessly focused on business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Own strategy and execution for all field marketing activities including factory tours, trade shows, guerrilla marketing, partner events, product launches, community days, VIP experiences, and original activations
Transform Machina's factories, products, and manufacturing technologies into compelling physical experiences, both onsite and in the field
Build out our factory showroom and create repeatable experiences that bring customers, partners, and decision-makers into the world of Machina Labs
Develop distinctive activations tailored to the audiences and business objectives of our defense and automotive businesses from technical experts and program leaders to senior executives
Serve as a creative and operational linchpin across marketing, collaborating with brand, content, communications, PR, social, and digital teams to bring integrated campaigns to life
Partner closely with BD and Executive Leadership to turn factory visits, demonstrations, and field experiences into a scalable engine for customer engagement and business development
Build, lead, and scale an events organization, including external production partners, vendors, and contractors
Collaborate with production, engineering, facilities, and compliance teams to execute ambitious experiences without compromising safety, operational priorities, or regulatory requirements
Extend beyond events to support adjacent marketing initiatives, including digital growth, community building, and partner marketing

Required Background & Experience

8+ years of field or experiential marketing experience in high-growth technology, manufacturing, automotive, defense, or similarly complex industries
Proven track record of creating memorable in-person experiences and building the processes and capabilities to scale them as a company grows
Strong personal point of view on experiential marketing. Doesn't simply execute a brief, but observes what resonates with target audiences and continuously improves the experience
Demonstrated ability to build trust and deliver results with cross-functional teams, external partners, and customers
Comfortable navigating complex physical environments, demanding logistics, competing priorities, and unexpected challenges
Resourceful with budgets and unwilling to accept industry norms around expensive, forgettable events. Finds creative ways to use the company's own products, people, and capabilities to achieve greater impact
Equally comfortable setting the strategy, managing the details, and rolling up their sleeves to make something happen

Preferred Qualifications

Background in robotics, AI, defense, automotive, advanced manufacturing, or industrial technology
Experience leading activations for complex B2B and B2G audiences, including enterprise and government buying processes
Experience producing large-scale product demonstrations, factory experiences, or events involving complex hardware and equipment
Los Angeles based preferred, or able to travel regularly for events, activations, and product launches (approximately 25%)

$110,000 - $140,000 a year

Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.

In addition to the provided base salary range, comprehensive benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision), PTO, and Stock Options.

jobs.title: Global Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

On the Waymo Marketing team, you will help to connect people with the magic and impact of Waymo's autonomous driving technology. Our team has the unique opportunity to not only grow Waymo's brand from the ground up, but to also build societal acceptance for autonomous driving technology for the first time in history. We build thoughtful marketing strategy, positioning, messaging and creative assets to deliver messages that matter to our audience, communicated through anything from video content, to social media interactions, to immersive physical experiences. We also shape Waymo's go-to-market initiatives, helping to transform Waymo into a thriving business with a growing user base.

In this hybrid role, you will report to our Head of Marketing.

You Will

Set the vision, strategy, and priorities for Product Marketing, ensuring the customer and market perspective informs Waymo’s product strategy, go-to-market decisions, and rider experience.
Serve as a strategic partner to Product, Engineering, and Operations leadership, influencing roadmaps, business priorities, and key decisions while driving alignment across teams.
Develop holistic marketing strategies for Waymo’s ride-hailing product and beyond, from positioning and launch through adoption and growth.
Lead product marketing for U.S. and international market launches, expansions, and ongoing market health, integrating consumer, brand, business, competitive, and product signals to identify opportunities and guide market priorities.
Build and develop a high-performing global Product Marketing team, fostering strong strategic thinking, execution, and collaboration to support Waymo’s rapid growth and evolving needs.

You Have

15+ years of product marketing or related marketing experience within consumer technology, including significant experience leading Product Marketing teams and complex consumer products or services.
Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing Product Marketing teams, setting a clear vision and priorities while fostering strong strategic thinking, execution, and cross-functional collaboration.
Deep experience partnering with Product leadership and influencing product strategy and roadmaps, bringing customer, market, and business perspectives into product development and key decisions.
Experience leading U.S. and international market launches and expansions, with the ability to synthesize consumer, brand, competitive, product, and business insights to inform market priorities.
Exceptional strategic judgment and executive influence, with the ability to navigate complexity, develop clear recommendations, and align senior stakeholders across Product, Marketing, Operations, and other functions.

We Prefer

Experience at a ride-hailing, marketplace, or app-based B2C company.
Concrete marketing experience driving the adoption of emerging technologies or new consumer behaviors, particularly where building understanding and trust is critical.
Track record across both established and early-stage products or markets.
Ability to balance long-term strategic thinking with near-term execution as business and product needs evolve.

Travel

Occasional travel to markets for research, and some travel for offsite meetings, approximately 10% of the time.

The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.

Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.

Salary Range

$249,000—$307,000 USD

jobs.description:
About The Role

It's a great time to join us at Airlines Reporting Corporation (ARC)! ARC accelerates the growth of global air travel by delivering forward-looking travel data, flexible distribution services and other innovative industry solutions. We are a leading travel intelligence company with the world’s largest, most comprehensive global airline ticket dataset, including more than 15 billion passenger flights. By working here, you can contribute to solutions and expertise that strengthen economies and enrich lives. We think big, embrace challenges and explore new ideas to lead the way for the travel industry.

We are looking for a talented Customer Marketing Lead
to apply broad and deep knowledge of ARC, its solutions, customers, and the global air travel industry to develop and manage product positioning, value propositions, target-market definitions, differentiated messaging, and customer marketing plans aligned with ARC’s broader marketing and communications strategy. You will conduct market research and collaborate across functions to define market segments. You will partner closely with Marketing and Communications, Product Management, and Sales to create product messaging, marketing plans, and sales and buyer enablement assets. You will lead initiatives and support peer-led efforts as needed, with teamwork essential to success. You will lead key customer engagement programs, including customer advocacy and win-loss research, requiring frequent customer interaction and strong communication and interpersonal skills. You will present findings and recommendations to leadership.

What You'll Get To Do

Conduct internal and external research to define customer needs and ensure they’re met with appropriate marketing content. Provide informational insights regarding customers, markets, and competitors to measure performance and support product development.
Build and maintain relationships with internal stakeholders and ARC partners to align customer marketing initiatives with business objectives.
Communicate regularly with customers to complete research and gain insight, including working group participation, webinar support and win/loss.
Own development of product positioning documents, value propositions, marketing materials for sales, and more. Coordinate with the broader marketing and communications team, product management and sales to develop marketing programs that drive adoption, engagement, retention and expansion.
Lead customer engagement efforts with the goal of capturing customer interest and needs, product attractiveness/feasibility and testimonials across solutions. This will entail meeting or interviewing key executives at ARC’s travel agency, airline, and other partners.

You'll Bring These Qualifications

4+ years of experience in customer marketing, product marketing or a related field.
Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent experience considered
Airline, travel agency or corporate travel experience strongly preferred, including knowledge of airline distribution and financial settlement.
Understanding of customer needs, travel data and industry trends and the ability to use these insights to guide marketing strategy.
Ability to develop clear positioning, value propositions and messaging that connect ARC’s products and solutions to customer needs.
Experience developing marketing strategies that support product launches, customer engagement, adoption and retention.
Strong research skills, including the ability to identify customer segments, develop personas and assess market opportunities.
Ability to collaborate across teams and translate product capabilities into meaningful customer benefits.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex workflows, integrations and application programming interfaces in language customers can understand.
Ability to summarize findings, present recommendations and communicate results to senior leaders and executives.

What We Can Offer You

Joining ARC means joining a team that is motivated, diverse, creative, collaborative and solutions-oriented. We think big, embrace challenges, and explore new ideas to lead the way for the travel industry.
Our employees value the hands-on learning and professional development opportunities that allow them to expand their skills and grow their career in new, dynamic ways.
ARC offers WorkFlex. WorkFlex is ARC’s hybrid work program which offers eligible employees the flexibility to work from home while also requiring in office workdays throughout the year to foster collaboration and connection throughout the organization. We’ve designed WorkFlex to enable employees to succeed and thrive while maintaining strong connections to one another and ARC - both of which are critical to our shared success.
We offer a highly competitive, comprehensive benefits package so you can worry less and focus on what truly matters. Please click here to review our benefits on our company website.
By joining ARC, you will partner with top minds in the industry as we use data and technology to innovate how the world travels.

The final offered salary will be based on several factors, including but not limited to the candidate’s depth of experience, skill set, qualifications, and internal pay equity. Hiring at the top end of the range would not be typical, allowing for meaningful future salary growth within the position.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
At Arcus, our mission is to empower anyone to build wealth by making investing accessible, affordable, and simple. The team behind Arcus previously built dYdX, helping power over $1.5 trillion in trading volume. Now we're bringing the world's financial markets onchain.

Built in partnership with Robinhood Chain and backed by a direct investment from Robinhood Crypto, Arcus brings crypto, stock tokens, commodities, and perpetual futures into one self-custodied account. Our vision is to build the world's best spot and perpetuals exchange - trusted, accessible, and reliable, with deep liquidity and accurate prices. Every asset, 24/7.

Experienced team: Google, Meta, Citadel, DRW, IMC Trading, Stripe, Coinbase, and more.
Leading backers and advisors: Andreessen Horowitz, Polychain Capital, Brian Armstrong, Fred Ehrsam, Naval Ravikant, Elad Gil, and more.

Join us in shaping the next generation of global financial markets!

→ Learn more about working at Arcus

Role Overview

We're looking for Product Marketing Lead who is also a trader who's also a strong communicator to own how Arcus explains what it ships to its users to generate excitement and engagement.

You turn what engineering builds into communications that traders understand and trust: blog posts, announcements, changelogs, docs, and launch threads. Every product update and incentive change passes through you first.

You're also the product team's best read on what traders actually think. You talk to traders directly, follow what they're saying across the chats, and bring back clear findings that shape product decisions and the roadmap.

This is a hands-on senior role that reports to the CBO and works daily with Product, Engineering, Growth, and Community.

Done well, this role is how Arcus earns trust with every launch. You'll be the voice that makes complex products feel clear, keeps traders confident in what's shipping, and turns real trader feedback into a sharper product for everyone.

Responsibilities

Launches: for every release you write the positioning, the announcement, the blog post, the X thread, and the docs update. You approve launch timing with Engineering so traders hear about a change before it goes live.
Prepare a short brief for each launch so KOLs, BD and regional communities have the right facts and assets.
In product copy: You own and sign off on all user facing copy within the product and app.
Eng to comms pipeline: you run the weekly changelog with Engineering and read it daily. Sensitive changes (fees, liquidations, withdrawals, points, security) get lead time and a reviewed draft. Nothing ships unannounced.
Announcement approvals. You draft, validate internally, and sign off on announcements. You decide what gets said, when, in which channels, and in what order.
Long-form content: use internal data to draft blog posts, product explainers, market-structure pieces and launch narratives that a trader would actually read.
Narrative and positioning: refine differentiation theses and roadmap into credible narrative positioning on why Arcus is different from competitors
Product signal: Talk to traders every day: whales, early contributors, active traders and people who churned. Transmit feedback on fills, listings, fees, UX, competitors, and other signal into structured synthesis for leadership
Get the most out of every partner, starting with Robinhood and the Robinhood Chain ecosystem. Set up co-marketing with each partner, then write and coordinate joint announcements, campaigns and content.
Incident / crisis comms: during rare market or product events, you write what we say, working with Engineering and Community. Community operates the information dissemination; you own the strategy.

Requirements

4+ years in product marketing, content or comms at a crypto-native or trading product, or an equivalent record of shipping launches.
You trade actively. You can explain funding rates, liquidations and fee tiers precisely, because a wrong sentence about them costs trust and money.
You've worked closely with engineers. You can read a changelog or spec, ask the right questions, and turn it into plain language without losing accuracy.
You write clearly and fast, in both long and short form.
You have a network of traders who reply to you and tell you the truth.
Good judgment about tone under pressure: you know when to explain, when to stay quiet, and when an apology makes things worse.

Nice To Haves

Launched products at a perp DEX (decentralized perpetual-futures exchange), a prediction market or a trading venue
Experience with points, rewards or token programs
Knowledge of Asian trader communities (Korea, Greater China)

Reporting directly to the Director of Marketing within the Brand Experience, Creative and Design Center of Excellence (COE), this role will support marketing strategy across key COPs including PCC + Radiation Oncology, Transplant, Neurology, Neurosurgery, ENT, Womens Health, OBGYN, GI, Surgery, Ophthalmology, Adult Psych and Urology. This individual will play a key leadership role in marketing planning and execution, translating strategy into actionable plans, manage workflows, measurement and deliverables.

Lead execution of the defined marketing strategy across tactical deliverables, including briefs, collateral, campaigns, and content calendars, ensuring consistency and adherence to strategic objectives, timely delivery and reporting to stakeholders
Ensure marketing plans elevate patient experience by incorporating patient narratives, care journey content, and clear, accessible information that supports patient decision-making and preparedness
Manage marketing deliverables, including briefs, collateral, campaigns, and content calendars aligned to strategies
Support management of overflow volume for priority projects as designated by the Senior Director
Apply audience segmentation and channel best practices under guidance of Senior Director, Relationship Lead and Marketing Director to maximize engagement and impact across patient and physician audiences
Partner with Digital teams to incorporate messaging, collateral, and search engine marketing (SEM) strategies into marketing plans to drive patient volume and service line growth
Assist in incorporating location-specific service line considerations to highlight access points, physician expertise, and key differentiators across NYULH markets
Oversee the integration of marketing tactics with broader institutional campaigns, ensuring consistent messaging

Execution & Tactics

Execute the strategy of the marketing function marketing deliverables - collateral, search engine marketing, messaging, owned channel opportunities (e.g., digital signage, email, ORG/EDU), multimedia, test and learn concepts) for portfolio
Write, design, and deliver marketing plans, ensuring timely delivery across channels and aligned to the strategic plan for the COP
Drive the development and tactical execution of marketing plans for new programs, procedures, and key recruitment efforts
Drive the execution of patient-focused content, including patient experience narratives, instructional and procedural videos, and physician profiles to highlight expertise and care differentiation
Ensure all marketing deliverables are developed and activated through defined marketing channels, including paid, owned, and digital platforms, in alignment with channel-specific requirements
Ensure collateral, messaging, and deliverables are consistent with brand standards and institutional guidelines

Collaboration & Influence

Collaborate with the Senior Director, Relationship Lead and Marketing Director by coordinating planning outputs to ensure they support institutional priorities, patient experience, clinical expertise, and service line differentiation
Collaborate with Channel Lead peers across Content Studio, Brand, Creative & Design, and Digital teams to lead collaborative marketing efforts with colleagues on email, digital signage, and other paid, earned and owned channels
Work with the Strategy, Digital, and Program Measurement COE to define campaign tracking requirements, support measurement setup, and inform ongoing campaign optimization
Prepare planning documentation and reporting for leadership review and inform decision-making and demonstrate outcomes
Work closely with the Senior Director, Relationship Lead and support members to ensure stakeholder-facing roles clearly communicate requests and objectives, and to translate the COP strategy into actionable, executable plans

Operational Excellence

Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability.

4 years of specific experience in contemporary digital media (websites, search, social, content marketing, video, mobile, CRM Strategy).

Experience in developing end-to-end customer journeys and designing automated marketing programs leveraging CRM data.

Integrate AI Skills and Agents in how we analyze and optimize our campaigns
Stay up-to-date on upcoming industry trends

Semi-annual bonuses for meeting key financial and operational goals

Job Summary

Working under general supervision of the Assistant Vice President, Communications & Marketing, the Director of Marketing & Advertising serves as a strategic leader within College Communications & Marketing (CCM) and is a key marketing partner to academic and enrollment leaders across Endicott College. The Director develops integrated marketing and advertising strategies that strengthen Endicott’s market position, increase visibility of its undergraduate and graduate academic offerings, and advance institutional enrollment and auxiliary revenue goals.

The Director will lead Endicott’s overarching advertising strategy across digital and traditional channels, ensuring investments are informed by institutional priorities, market conditions, data, and defined measures of success. Another primary responsibility is establishing the strategic foundation for how the College brings its programs to market, including positioning frameworks, audience strategies, value propositions, and campaign plans across advertising, web, print, digital, recruitment communications, and content.

Working closely with the Brand Manager, Undergraduate Admission, the Director of Admission Communication, and the Assistant Vice President of Graduate Enrollment, the Director will help steward undergraduate and graduate enrollment marketing and lead major marketing initiatives from strategy through implementation and assessment.

About Endicott College

Endicott College is a vibrant community located on Boston’s North Shore, with a beautiful oceanfront campus in Beverly, Massachusetts. We’re known for combining academic excellence with hands-on learning, and we take pride in fostering a supportive environment for both students and employees.

Working at Endicott means joining a close-knit campus community where your contributions matter and where collaboration, creativity, and professional growth are valued.

Benefits

To learn more about our employee benefits click here.

Key Outcomes

30
% of Time:
Integrated Marketing Strategy & Institutional Priorities

Develop and lead annual and long-term marketing strategies that advance College priorities, including enrollment, institutional visibility, engagement, and revenue growth.

Translate institutional goals into actionable marketing plans that establish audiences, positioning, messaging, channels, investment, timelines, and measures of success.
Lead marketing strategy for major College initiatives and emerging priorities, bringing together advertising, brand, creative, content, web, social media, and communications as appropriate.
Evaluate marketing requests and opportunities against institutional priorities, audience needs, revenue or enrollment potential, available resources, and expected impact.
Monitor market conditions, audience behavior, competitive activity, and marketing trends to identify opportunities and inform College marketing strategy.

30% of Time: Advertising, Digital Marketing & Performance

Lead Endicott’s advertising strategy across digital and traditional channels, partnering with an external agency on paid search, paid social, and digital display while directly overseeing out-of-home, print, broadcast, and other advertising opportunities.
Manage advertising agencies, media partners, vendors, and other external marketing relationships.
Establish KPIs and reporting frameworks for major campaigns and regularly communicate performance, insights, and recommendations to College leadership and campus partners.
Ensure paid campaigns are supported by strong creative, content, web experiences, and conversion pathways.
Evaluate new advertising channels, partnerships, sponsorships, and promotional opportunities based on audience fit, institutional goals, cost, and expected return.

25% of Time: Enrollment & Academic Program Marketing

Lead integrated marketing strategy supporting undergraduate and graduate enrollment in close partnership with Enrollment Management and academic leadership.
Develop annual undergraduate and graduate marketing plans informed by enrollment goals, priority audiences, market opportunity, program demand, and performance data.
Develop marketing strategies for new and priority academic programs, including audience identification, positioning, value propositions, competitive differentiation, launch strategy, and campaign planning.
Partner with Undergraduate Admission, Graduate Enrollment, academic leaders, and CCM colleagues to align advertising, recruitment communications, web, print, digital, and content around a cohesive prospective-student journey.
Use enrollment and marketing data to identify opportunities and recommend changes to targeting, investment, channels, messaging, creative, and conversion strategies.

15% of Time: Marketing Content, Web & Audience Experience

Continually assess whether Endicott has the content, creative assets, web experiences, and audience pathways necessary to support its marketing priorities.
Partner with CCM’s creative, social, and web teams to identify gaps and establish priorities for new marketing assets.
Partner with CCM’s content, creative, social, video, and photography teams to identify gaps in the College’s marketing asset library and establish priorities for new asset development, with particular attention to priority audiences and programs.
Conduct ongoing audits of Endicott’s marketing and enrollment web presence and recommend new pages, landing pages, content improvements, audience pathways, calls to action, and other enhancements.
Ensure major advertising and marketing initiatives have the content and digital infrastructure necessary to effectively move audiences from awareness to action.
Be an active participant in the life of the College by attending and supporting major events such as Commencement, Homecoming, and other all-hands-on-deck gatherings. As a member of the leadership team, model a strong commitment to community engagement.
Other duties as assigned

Reporting Structure

Reports to the Assistant Vice President of Communications & Marketing.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Supervises the Brand Manager and is responsible for setting priorities, assigning and overseeing work, providing coaching and performance feedback, supporting professional development, conducting performance evaluations, and participating in hiring and onboarding as appropriate.

Strategic Marketing Leadership

Connects institutional and enrollment priorities, audience insights, market conditions, and data to develop focused, actionable marketing strategies with clear objectives and measures of success.

Consultative Leadership & Partnership

Builds credibility and trust with academic, enrollment, and institutional leaders; asks the right questions to uncover underlying needs and opportunities; and translates complex priorities into effective marketing strategies.

Audience & Market Orientation

Approaches marketing from the perspective of the audience rather than the tactic; uses market research, competitive context, audience behavior, and institutional strengths to inform positioning and strategy.

Data-Informed Decision Making

Establishes meaningful measures of success, evaluates marketing and advertising performance, identifies actionable insights, and uses data to optimize strategy, investment, channels, and creative.

Integrated Thinking

Sees how advertising, brand, web, content, communications, enrollment communications, and the prospective-student journey work together; brings the right people and channels together around a shared strategy.

Moves complex initiatives from strategy through execution and assessment; establishes clear objectives, roles, priorities, timelines, and accountability while managing multiple concurrent initiatives effectively.

Influence & Communication

Communicates strategies, recommendations, and performance insights clearly and persuasively; facilitates productive conversations and can build alignment among stakeholders with different priorities and levels of marketing expertise.

Works effectively within a multidisciplinary environment and values the expertise of brand, creative, content, digital, communications, enrollment, and academic colleagues; provides clear strategic direction without unnecessarily owning every aspect of execution.

Experience developing positioning, audience, value proposition, competitive differentiation, and go-to-market frameworks.
Demonstrated ability to establish KPIs, analyze marketing performance, and translate data into actionable recommendations.

Experience marketing multiple programs, products, services, or audience segments with differing goals and customer journeys.
Experience identifying content and creative asset needs and providing strategic direction for video, photography, and other marketing production.
Experience working with CRM, marketing automation, analytics, and/or enrollment management platforms.
Experience supporting revenue-generating initiatives, events, venues, or other consumer-facing offerings.
Experience supervising, mentoring, or developing marketing professionals.
Familiarity with higher education enrollment trends, prospective student behavior, and the evolving digital marketing landscape.

About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About The Role

We're hiring a Head of Growth Marketing to own how Rho wins new customers across every acquisition channel: paid search, paid social, connected TV, outbound, direct mail, lifecycle, SEO and AEO, referrals, and affiliates. You'll be the growth PM for the entire funnel, deciding what to test, proving what works, and moving budget toward it.

Growth at Rho runs as a pod with two leads. You'll lead growth marketing in partnership with our growth engineering lead: you shape what we test and why, and growth engineering builds it and makes it scale. You'll work alongside a team that ships landing pages, data pipelines, and outbound systems in days, AI routines that run every morning, and a BDR team that calls new leads within minutes.

You're accountable for new funded customers and the gross profit they bring. Cost per funded customer, payback, and experiment velocity are how your work gets judged.

Key responsibilities

Own Rho's growth target for new funded customers and gross profit, and break it into channel goals each owner in the pod can run with.
Build and run the experimentation program: a one-page brief for every idea (audience, channel, copy variants, tracking, and the scale or kill threshold), a shared tracker, and a Friday retro. Ideas ship in days.
Turn ideas from across the company, from the CEO to the sales floor, into experiments that marketing operations and growth engineering can stand up quickly, and own the follow-through.
Design holdouts and incrementality tests that show which channels create new customers, and move the next dollar based on the results.
Own paid strategy across Google Ads, LinkedIn, Meta, and connected TV, including agency partners, with a clear cost-per-funded-customer and payback bar for each channel.
Lift conversion from first click to funded account through landing page and onboarding tests with design and engineering, from comparison tables to one-click email capture.
Shape lifecycle and nurture so every lead gets the right message at the right moment, and approved customers fund and start using Rho.
Partner with Growth BDRs and account executives on lead routing, speed to lead, outbound plays, and which sources turn into customers.
Work with data and marketing operations on attribution, conversion tracking back to ad platforms, and the weekly scorecard the team runs on.
Agentify the growth loop: build and run AI agents and daily routines that pull funnel and CRO data, generate hypotheses, draft variants, and report results, so the team spends its time on judgment, not busywork.

Requirements

5-7+ years in growth or performance marketing, including at least two years leading growth at a B2B, fintech, or high-velocity SaaS company. You can name the numbers you moved.
Revenue-oriented first: funded customers and gross profit are what get you out of bed.
Has run a high-volume experimentation program and kept it both fast and rigorous.
Hands-on experience designing incrementality tests and holdouts, and the ability to explain to a CEO what last-click reporting misses.
Hands on across paid search, paid social, lifecycle email, and outbound; you build a campaign yourself when that's the fastest path.
Comfortable in SQL and modern data and marketing tools.
You build with AI agents yourself (Claude Code or similar). Your first move on a repetitive task is to agentify it, not hire for it.
Leads through influence: you've partnered with engineering as a peer and rallied a cross-functional team around one goal. Experience managing people is a plus.
Comfortable working inside a regulated business: exact disclosures, verified claims, and compliance review as part of the shipping process.
Based in New York City and excited to work in office with the team.

We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. Track conversion from MQL to meeting to opportunity by program, and diagnose where it breaks.

Route play-triggered leads directly to Sales with context, and measure each play against the pipeline it creates.

Build evergreen cross-sell programs between Workforce Compliance products.

.

new_jobs.title: Marketing Operations Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Talkdesk competes in a market where the quality of execution separates companies that grow efficiently from those that spend more to get the same result. Marketing Operations is where that execution lives. This role exists to ensure that every dollar of marketing spend, every campaign, every event, and every account-based program translates into pipeline with zero friction. That requires a system built for precision where the right prospect reaches the right person at the right time, consistently and by design.
You sit inside the Marketing team, with close partnerships across Sales and RevOps. The marketers running campaigns, events, and account-based programs are your primary stakeholders. When the system works, their work converts.
In practice, that means owning the full operational surface of marketing technology: administering and continuously improving the tools that make up our GTM stack, building and maintaining the integrations that keep data moving cleanly between systems, designing the orchestrations that automate account and contact engagement, ensuring the enrichment and data integrity standards that make every downstream decision reliable. This is an interdependent system, and this person keeps it running as a coherent, high-performing whole.
What You'll Own

Account-Based Marketing Orchestration:

Serve as the technical owner of our ABM orchestration layer. Translate signals from our intent platform into automated, sequenced actions across our marketing automation platform and CRM, working closely with campaign and field marketing teams to ensure the right programs reach the right accounts at the right moment. Getting this infrastructure right is one of the highest-impact contributions this role makes to the business.

Marketing Technology Foundation:

Own the day-to-day health of our martech systems and the workflows, API calls, integrations, and syncs that connect them to keep prospect data moving accurately through the funnel. When something breaks or underperforms, you diagnose it, fix it, and document the resolution so it does not recur.

Agentic AI Workflow Engineering:

Design and build automated workflows that use AI capabilities to evaluate qualitative signals, such as demo request notes, intent activity, and unstructured form inputs, alongside firmographic data to produce dynamic lead scores and routing decisions. You write the API calls, design the orchestration logic, test against edge cases, and iterate based on conversion outcomes. Experience shipping something to production is the bar.

Enrichment and Insights:

Build and manage the workflows that construct a complete, account-level intelligence profile from the moment a prospect engages. That means aggregating first-party behavioral signals, third-party intent data, firmographic context, and web research into a unified view that captures not just the individual contact but the broader buying committee: who across the account is engaging, with what content, and what their activity suggests about organizational priorities and pain points. That intelligence surfaces in the systems where sales and marketing work, so every follow-up is informed, relevant, and timed to the account's buying journey.

System Documentation and Enablement:

Every workflow you build or modify gets documented: field mapping dictionaries, AI orchestration logic, routing rule change logs. Beyond documentation, you actively invest in making the marketing team more self-sufficient, building self-service reporting and dashboards that allow marketers to check campaign performance, list quality, or lead status independently, and creating resources that allow colleagues to troubleshoot routine tasks and leverage AI tools without filing a request. An empowered marketing team operates with greater speed and confidence, and this role contributes meaningfully to that outcome.

Who You Are

You operate with a high degree of autonomy. You are embedded in the relevant standups, attentive to system performance, and typically ahead of issues before they surface as escalations. Your manager will set context and priorities; the execution is yours to own.
You are invested in the success of the Marketing team. You understand that the campaigns, events, and programs your colleagues execute are only as effective as the systems that support them. Leads from a field event that go unrouted, an ABM sequence that executes against incomplete data, or a high-intent inbound request that experiences significant delay before reaching an SDR all represent measurable pipeline impact. You approach your work with that accountability in mind.
You are technically strong and collaborative by nature. Marketers, Sales and RevOps are close partners. You understand their workflows well enough to anticipate where system gaps will affect their work, and communicate clearly when something is broken, when it is fixed, and why. Strong cross-functional relationships are central to this role.
You see the work through to completion. You build, test, document, and close the loop. When something you own regresses, you identify it first.
What We're Looking For

Required
3 to 5 years in B2B SaaS Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or a systems-adjacent role
Hands-on marketing automation and CRM administration, including configuring and maintaining MAP-to-CRM syncs
Demonstrated ability to build and deploy an automated workflow that calls external APIs, whether webhooks, REST APIs, or LLM endpoints, in a production environment
Native fluency in B2B funnel mechanics: MQL definitions, lifecycle stage transitions, opportunity lifecycles, and attribution models
Experience coaching or enabling non-technical stakeholders on new tools, AI workflows, or self-service reporting

Strong Signal
Hands-on administrative experience with intent data platforms, routing engines, and ABM orchestration
Prior experience building LLM-powered workflows for lead scoring, routing, or qualification
Comfort reading and writing JSON, working with REST APIs, and debugging integration errors independently

How We'll Measure Success

The through-line across all of it is pipeline efficiency: more of the right prospects converting into pipeline from the programs already running, with less manual intervention and less fallout.
30 days: Full audit of marketing automation-to-CRM field mapping is complete, ownership of inbound routing rules is established, and current ABM workflow patterns are mapped to identify key automation opportunities.
60 days: First agentic AI workflow is deployed to staging or production. At least one major ABM orchestration sequence that previously required manual steps is automated. An initial self-service enablement resource or dashboard is delivered to the marketing team.
90 days and beyond: Lead sync exception rate is at target with a monitoring process that catches regressions before Sales does. ABM orchestration operates as a reliable service layer that campaign and field marketers can brief and trust to execute. Marketing colleagues actively leverage self-service tools and AI workflows independently.
Application Question

Required with your resume (200 words max):

A high-intent prospect submits a demo request but never reaches the assigned SDR in the CRM. Walk us through your exact diagnostic process: which logs you check first, how you trace the break across the marketing automation-to-CRM sync and inbound routing rules, how you validate the fix, and how you would design an agentic step to evaluate the prospect's form submission notes for priority routing.

Job Summary

The Marketing and Sales Representative (MSR) will promote and sell OAL lottery products. This position is responsible for overseeing a designated field territory, ensuring consistent and continuous service to our retailers. The MSR will act as the primary customer service and account representative, serving as the main point of contact between retailers and the OAL. In this role, the MSR will train retailers on the lottery games and address any complaints or issues that may arise between retailers and customers. Additionally, the MSR will work to secure new business and ensure that new license applications are completed. The MSR will also collaborate closely with vendor partners to maintain the ongoing workflow of OAL as needed.

Primary Responsibilities

Serves as a customer service representative and liaison for ASL within an assigned territory. Identifies route requirements and retailer needs, analyzes ticket usage to determine current demands, and coordinates the placement of ASL promotional materials and supplies. Travels extensively to vendors and retailers to deliver promotional material, provide training, and offer other necessary services. Utilizes a system to deliver and track tickets, reconciles ticket usage with inventory, adjusts inventory levels, and reallocates tickets to other retailers as needed. Ensures proper activation for financial accountability and billing purposes. Analyzes store layouts to recommend the most effective placement of point-of-sale and promotional items. Instructs retailers on strategies to increase sales, motivates them to promote ASL products, and suggests suitable promotional strategies or programs. Recruits and secures new retailers, ensuring the completion and compliance of licensing applications. Trains both new and existing retailers on instant games, other ASL games, and the operation of Lottery validation equipment. Maintains retailer centers to ensure they are presentable and serve as effective sales tools. Identifies retailer issues and plans appropriate actions to resolve them, ensuring the rapid delivery of special ticket orders to retailers. Ensures compliance with ASL rules and regulations. Completes accounting, security, and sales reports, and meets regularly with the assigned Regional Sales Manager to provide updates and information.

Skilled in negotiating and resolving conflicts while maintaining positive working relationships.

Ability to analyze sales data, identify trends, and make data-driven decisions.

Familiarity with marketing strategies, promotional campaigns, and brand management.

A strong customer service mindset with the ability to respond to retailer and customer needs in a professional and timely manner.

Experience in dedicated sales route management or direct customer interaction is a plus.

Strong verbal and written communication skills are necessary.

The ability to work independently without direct supervision.

Effective Time Management And Organizational Skills Are Essential.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and basic office equipment (printers, copiers, fax machines).

A bachelor’s degree is preferable, but a high school diploma plus 3 years of sales or customer service experience can be substituted.

Valid Driver’s License.

new_jobs.title: Marketing Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Marketing Specialist

HydroJug — Brand Marketing
Location: Ogden, UT
Reports to: VP of Marketing
Team: Brand Marketing

ABOUT HYDROJUG

HydroJug built a category and a community around hydration as a daily ritual. Our marketing team is the customer — they know the brands, the gyms, the creators, the moments. That insider fluency is why the work lands. We're expanding into new categories and new consumer segments, and we need that same engine running on the new side of the house.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

You won't be coordinating launches for a community you study. You'll be coordinating launches for communities you're already part of. Our existing marketing works because the team lives in the world it markets to — same gyms, same feeds, same creators. The new category will only work the same way: with someone whose network is already in the spaces we're entering, who can tell us which podcast just blew up before the rest of the internet catches on, and who knows which brands are doing the most interesting work in lifting, hybrid athletics, run, hunt and outdoor, combat sport, and performance wellness. This is a specialist role on purpose. You'll own a compressed version of what a much larger team owns on our established side — seeding and influencer first, brand partnerships second, then events, content, and the rest as the program scales.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN (IN PRIORITY SEQUENCE)

Priority 1 — Product seeding & influencer relationships (first 90 days)
Build the PR list for the new category from scratch — tiered by network economy, not follower count.
Run all four customization tiers (generic → one-of-one) against the right recipients.
Own the seed → follow-up → track → convert workflow for every send. No charitable donations.
Open warm channels with creators across our priority spaces: lifting and hybrid, run, outdoor and hunt, combat sport, and performance wellness.

Priority 2 — Brand partnerships (months 3–6)
Identify the brand counterparts that fit alongside our existing partnership portfolio in these spaces.
Open conversations with the operators (not the agencies) at those brands.
Build the institutional seeding lane — gyms, teams, races, schools — where attention concentrates in these communities.

Priority 3 — Events, content, and adjacent motions (months 6+)
Stand up the event calendar in coordination with the Events Coordinator.
Brief UGC and Social on what reads as native in these spaces — what to do and what not to do.
Become the in-house translator: every team that touches the new category comes to you first.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The non-negotiable credential is demonstrated immersion in and access to the communities
and culture surrounding the spaces above. That shows up as:
An active, real network of creators, athletes, and brand operators in those spaces — the kind where DMs get answered the same day.
Lived participation in at least one (ideally more) of our target spaces: lifting, hybrid and HYROX, run, hunt and outdoor, combat sport, or performance wellness.
Fluent reads on the brand landscape in these categories — you can name the five brands doing the best work right now and the three about to break.
A track record of putting product in the right hands or building programs that earned attention from these communities. What "experience" looks like is flexible. 2–4 years in influencer, partnerships, brand, or creator-side work is typical. We care more about your network and judgment than your title history.

OPERATING STYLE WE HIRE FOR

You run on calendar discipline. A missed send is cheaper than a bad send.
You build relationships, not contact lists. The litmus test is whether the recipient stays if a competitor offers 20% more.
You customize. Generic PR boxes are the floor we're trying to clear.
You track conversion, not volume. Seeds earn relationships, not impressions.
You're opinionated and you write it down.

WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

VP of Marketing (direct manager), Influencer Manager, Strategic Brand Partnerships, Social, UGC, Events, Retention, Performance Marketing, and the Product team driving the new-category launches.

HOW YOU'LL BE MEASURED

Active PR list size and tier mix in the new category
Conversion rate of seeds → ambassador, earned content, or partnership
Cost per earned impression in the new category
Brand-partner pipeline opened and activated
Quality of cross-functional collaboration (named, not surveyed)

About Tidal Vision

We believe that sustainability should not require customers to compromise on price, convenience, or performance. Our mission is to create positive & systemic impact for the critical industries that sustain life. We value innovation and take pride in challenging the status-quo; we choose to view obstacles as opportunities. We value new ideas and encourage the team to apply creativity and invent new solutions to meet challenging demands. We foster open, direct communication, and a collaborative working environment through our unique approach to work culture. We value our employees and demonstrate that through our compensation and benefits programs and opportunities for growth and development.

About Tidal Grow AgriScience

Tidal Grow AgriScience develops next-generation agricultural technologies designed to improve crop performance, nutrient efficiency, and grower profitability. By translating advanced chitosan science into practical, scalable products, we create innovative agricultural solutions that integrate seamlessly into modern farming operations to deliver higher yields with more efficient inputs.

About Tidal Vision’s Unique Work Culture

Tidal Vision strives to build and invest in the highest performing and most innovative team. We put our people and customers above process, avoid company-wide rules as much as possible, and have the courage to take unusual approaches to advance our mission. With this approach, we believe we can create a more flexible, fun, stimulating, creative, collaborative, and innovative organization.

Our commitment to developing, practicing and promoting direct and open communication, responsibility and freedom, and leading with and seeking context is a responsibility for every role at Tidal Vision.

Job Summary

The Director, Portfolio Strategy & Product Marketing leads the commercial strategy and market success of Tidal Grow AgriScience’s product portfolio. The role owns segmentation, targeting, positioning, pricing, channel strategy, label and claims strategy, launch planning, and lifecycle commercialization.

This role is a critical member of the Product organization, working alongside Product Management and R&D to shape and commercialize Tidal Grow AgriScience's product portfolio. As the portfolio's commercial leader, the Director drives market strategy, positioning, pricing, channel strategy, launch planning, and lifecycle commercialization to ensure products achieve successful market adoption and long-term growth.

Essential Job Functions

Lead portfolio commercialization strategy across crop nutrition, biostimulant, and crop protection markets.
Own segmentation, targeting, positioning, value propositions, pricing architecture, and channel strategy.
Own the commercial direction of each product from development through launch and lifecycle management.
Own label and claims strategy, partnering with Regulatory on registrations, substantiation, and compliance.
Partner with Product Managers to translate technical capabilities, efficacy data, and customer needs into commercially successful products.
Partner with Marketing to establish promotional strategy, message hierarchy, proof points, and sales-enablement priorities; Marketing owns creative development and execution.
Build market, customer, competitive, pricing, and channel intelligence into portfolio plans, business cases, forecasts, and commercialization decisions.
Work with the Chief Product Officer on product vision, roadmap priorities, portfolio architecture, and investment decisions.
Align Product Management, R&D, Commercial Ag Science, Regulatory, Marketing, Sales, and Operations around commercialization plans and market outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, agronomy, agricultural economics, marketing, business, crop science, or a related field.
At least 15 years of progressive experience in agricultural product marketing, portfolio strategy, product management, market development, or commercial leadership.
Commercial leadership experience across both crop nutrition/fertilizer and crop protection.
Proven success leading segmentation, positioning, pricing, channel, launch, lifecycle, and portfolio strategies for agricultural products.
Strong understanding of grower economics, agricultural distribution, retail channels, product labels, claims, and commercialization requirements.
Ability to translate technical and field-performance data into differentiated value propositions and commercially compelling strategies.
Strong financial acumen and experience developing value-based pricing, channel economics, and product business cases.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive decisions without direct authority.
Executive-level communication, judgment, and presence.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or advanced degree in agribusiness, marketing, agricultural economics, agronomy, or a related field.
Experience leading a multi-product portfolio within an established agricultural input company.
Experience launching and scaling innovative or technically differentiated agricultural products.
Experience across distributor, retailer, and direct-to-grower channels.
Success operating in an entrepreneurial or rapidly scaling business.

Own the CRM strategy, customer experience vision, operational framework, and long-term scalability
across lifecycle, loyalty, acquisition, automation, CDP-enabled personalization, and AI-enhanced marketing. This role sets the vision for hyper-personalized customer journeys at scale, builds the roadmap, and ensures CRM becomes a fun, future-forward growth engine that customers actually feel.

Core Responsibilities

CRM Strategy & Direction

Define and own the overall CRM strategy across lifecycle, personalization, loyalty, retention, acquisition, automation, and customer experience.
Establish strategic guardrails for segmentation, testing, cadence, and channel mix.
Identify optimization opportunities at scale (new use cases, automation, advanced targeting).
Own customer journey mapping, journey planning, and journey execution across acquisition, onboarding, engagement, loyalty, winback, reactivation, and retention moments.
Build and own the CRM roadmap, ensuring lifecycle initiatives, CDP capabilities, automations, testing plans, AI enhancements, and personalization use cases ladder up to a clear long-term vision.
Champion hyper-personalization at scale by turning customer data, behavioral signals, lifecycle triggers, and AI-powered decisioning into relevant, timely, and genuinely delightful customer experiences.

Team Leadership & Oversight

Manage, develop, and set clear priorities for the Senior Digital Marketing Specialists, ensuring the team has the skills, context, tools, and accountability needed to deliver consistently.

Coach team members on prioritization, decision-making, operational tradeoffs, platform ownership, and cross-functional leadership.
Define clear ownership across roles, create strong execution standards, and ensure work can scale without constant escalation.
Build a team culture focused on continuous learning, proactive problem-solving, documentation, and shared knowledge across channels and platforms.

Operational Excellence at Scale

Ensure CRM operations are scalable, repeatable, and resilient across all markets.
Own the day-to-day health and long-term evolution of CRM platforms, including administration standards, access, integrations, releases, feature adoption, documentation, and platform governance.
Own high-level process design, governance, QA, monitoring, incident response, and documentation standards.
Oversee risk management related to launches, outages, compliance, platform dependencies, and ecosystem changes.
Manage CRM platform, agency, and technology vendors by defining scopes, timelines, deliverables, service levels, QA expectations, documentation, budgets, and accountability.
Set a high bar for vendor partnership: vendors should accelerate execution and expertise, not become the sole source of truth for strategy, platform knowledge, testing, validation, or day-to-day decision-making.

Offer Decisioning & Personalization

Own the offer decisioning strategy and operating model, including eligibility, suppression, prioritization, arbitration, contact rules, testing, measurement, and governance.
Partner with loyalty, analytics, technology, merchandising, ecommerce, and operations to ensure offers are accurate, relevant, financially responsible, and executable across channels.
Translate customer signals, lifecycle stage, affinity, behavior, and business rules into scalable next-best-action and next-best-offer experiences.

Channel, Device & Ecosystem Leadership

Maintain current expertise in email, SMS/MMS, mobile push, in-app, web, app, paid-media audiences, and emerging CRM channels, including evolving best practices in omnichannel integration, AI, privacy, and security.
Monitor and prepare for ecosystem changes—including iOS and Android upgrades, device-level privacy controls, deliverability requirements, consent expectations, attribution changes, app capabilities, and platform policy updates—and translate them into clear business and technical actions.
Evaluate and responsibly adopt new capabilities in automation, predictive analytics, AI-assisted orchestration, and agentic workflows within defined governance and measurement guardrails.

Enterprise Data & Pipeline Readiness

Proactively identify and assess relevant customer, transaction, behavioral, digital, retail, loyalty, service, and operational data available across the company.
Partner with data, analytics, engineering, technology, product, ecommerce, retail, compliance, and business owners to define source-of-truth requirements and make usable data available to CRM systems.
Ensure data pipelines provide a clean, complete, timely, validated, and well-documented entry into CRM, CDP, decisioning, reporting, and activation platforms, with monitoring and clear ownership for quality issues.
Establish data-quality standards for identity resolution, consent, customer attributes, event definitions, taxonomy, suppression logic, deduplication, latency, reconciliation, and downstream usability.
Create an escalation and remediation process for data gaps, broken feeds, schema changes, unexpected volume shifts, and platform discrepancies before they affect customers or reporting.

Performance Management & Insights

Set expectations for KPIs, reporting frameworks, and insights across CRM.
Translate performance trends into strategic recommendations for leadership.
Ensure testing frameworks align with broader business goals—not just channel metrics.

Cross-Functional & Executive Alignment

Act as the primary CRM stakeholder for leadership, technology, analytics, creative, brand, acquisition, operations, retail, vendors, agencies, platform partners, and external partners.
Align CRM priorities with:
Brand strategy
Loyalty initiatives
Personalization roadmaps

Represent CRM in roadmap planning, resourcing discussions, acquisition planning, customer experience visioning, and GTM initiatives to ensure cross-functional teams are building toward the same customer-first future.
Partner cross-functionally to manage CRM vendor inputs, translate business needs into clear requirements, hold partners accountable to outcomes, and ensure internal teams retain ownership of strategy, customer experience, and decision-making.

Create and manage cross-functional workflows and recurring meeting cadences to track progress, surface findings, resolve risks and dependencies, document decisions, and clearly report strategic recommendations and outcomes to leadership and key stakeholders.
